# laravel_cloud_environment_resend (Resource)

Connects Resend email sending to an environment, with a new sending key or one reused from another environment. The organization must have Resend connected, and from_address must be on a domain verified in Resend. Destroying this detaches Resend from the environment and deletes its sending key unless another environment still uses it.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "laravel_cloud_environment_resend" "example" {
  environment_id = laravel_cloud_environment.example.id
  from_address   = "hello@example.com"
  from_name      = "Example"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `environment_id` (String) Environment ID.
- `from_address` (String) Sender email address, on a domain verified in Resend.
- `from_name` (String) Sender name (max 255 chars).

### Optional

- `key_name` (String) Name of the sending key created for the environment (max 255 chars). Defaults to a name the platform derives from the environment. With reuse_key_id, this reports the reused key's name and cannot be set. Changing it creates a new key.
- `reuse_key_id` (String) ID of another environment's sending key to reuse instead of creating one. Changing it forces a new integration. The API never reports it back, so an imported integration leaves it null.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Same as environment_id.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import laravel_cloud_environment_resend.example "{environment_id}"
```
